prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on your home, budget, timing, and how important long warranties or high-efficiency equipment are to you. I can, however, help you find highly rated contractors and tell you exactly what to look for so you get a good install.

If you want immediate names (common, well-reviewed options in the Atlanta area)
- Coolray Heating & Air — large local presence, lots of reviews, offers 24/7 service.
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning — national firm with local branches and financing options.
- One Hour Heating & Air (and related Neighborly brands) — quick-response model and many local franchises.
- Local independent contractors — often have better prices and more personalized service; check reviews and credentials.

How to pick the best one for your AC replacement
1. Get at least 3 written estimates. Compare scope, equipment brand/model, SEER rating, labor warranty, and total price.
2. Require a Manual J load calculation. That determines correct system size for your home — not “rule of thumb” sizing.
3. Check credentials: licensed in Georgia, insured (liability & workers’ comp), and preferably NATE‑certified technicians.
4. Ask about permits and code compliance. The contractor should pull permits and arrange inspections if required.
5. Compare warranties: manufacturer parts warranty vs. installer labor warranty (look for at least 1–10 years labor).
6. Read recent customer reviews (Google, Yelp, BBB) and ask for references for similar installations.
7. Ask about ductwork and indoor air quality: will they seal/repair ducts? Do you need a new coil or thermostat?
8. Confirm timeline and cleanup policy (removal of old equipment, disposal).

Questions to ask each contractor
- Will you perform a Manual J and provide the report?
- What brand and model do you recommend and why?
- What is the system’s SEER rating and estimated seasonal efficiency?
- What are total costs (equipment, labor, permits, disposal)? Any hidden fees?
- What warranties come with the equipment and the installation?
- Do you offer financing? What are the terms?
- Who will perform the install and are they NATE-certified?

Typical cost ranges (Atlanta, ballpark)
- Basic central AC replacement (single-family, existing ductwork): roughly $3,500–$7,500.
- Higher-efficiency systems, upgrades, or new ductwork: $7,500–$12,000+.
(Exact price depends on home size, SEER, brand, and ductwork condition. Get written bids.)

Brands to consider
- Higher-end: Trane, Carrier, Lennox — often better durability/efficiency but pricier.
- Mid-range: Rheem, Ruud, Goodman — good balance of price/performance.
Pick a reputable brand and focus on correct sizing and quality of installation — that matters as much as the brand.

If you want, I can:
- Narrow to the top-rated contractors near you if you tell me your Atlanta neighborhood or ZIP code.
- Give a checklist you can print and take to estimates.
- Help compare written estimates you receive.
